questions.content:
With three points, explain why a ship does not sink in water while the coin sinks?
(i). __________________
(ii). __________________
(iii). __________________

media.alt: Complete unchanged original physics paper page 6.

questions.marksProvenance: Associated source guide page(s) [4]; original paper section totals retained separately.
questions.markIncrementProvenance: Independent half-mark self-assessment granularity; official substep increments are not asserted.
questions.answerKey: A hollow ship has an average density below water; its large submerged volume displaces sufficient water to provide an upthrust equal to its weight at floating equilibrium. A compact coin normally has density above water, so even fully submerged its buoyant force is less than its weight.
questions.markingGuide: Source guide3points/marks; independent scientifically corrected explanation, one mark each for average density/hollow volume, displacement/upthrust balance, and why the denser coin sinks.
